a: They suffered loss, perished, and became wretched.
‘The hands of Abu Lahab’: the two well-known limbs.
Abu Lahab: the nickname of ‘Abd al-‘Uzza ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib, the uncle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.
Abu Lahab: the nickname of ‘Abd al-‘Uzza ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib, the uncle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.
‘Tabba’: he suffered loss, perished, and became wretched.
It may be negative or interrogative.
‘Ma aghna ‘anhu’: it did not suffice him and did not benefit him against Allah’s punishment when it befell him.
‘An: a preposition conveying the meaning of causation.
Mal (wealth): what is owned of goods, real estate, money, or animals.
‘Ma’: it may be relative or verbal-noun (masdariyya).
‘Ma kasaba’: what is meant here is his child.
‘Dhata lahab’: as a description of Hell.
Lahab (flame): what rises from the fire as if it were a tongue, or the blazing of the fire and its kindling.

‘The carrier of firewood’: she was called so because she used to bring thorny branches and throw them at night on the path of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him; and she was a talebearer who kindled the fire of enmity among people.
Cut branches of trees and thorns.
A preposition in the meaning of ‘ala (on).
A tie with which something is bound.
A preposition conveying clarification of the kind, or clarification of what is vague before ‘min’ or in its context.
